It also covers the client's refused-answer path: a result the Host refuses with LOOPBACK_REQUIRED emits `remote/answer-refused` and keeps the event stream, while any other refusal still ends the generation. Covers `remote/call-denied`: emitted with the endpoint and reason on `remote-access/denied`, not on other failures, and a throwing listener leaves the call result unchanged. Covers `$liftDenials`: one handler at a time; a refused unary call is sent exactly once more only when the handler resolves true, and the caller receives that second outcome; false, a throwing handler or a withdrawn handler hands the refusal to the caller, and `remote/call-denied` is emitted only for a refusal the caller receives. It also covers the stream lift (a refused stream open is reopened once with the uplink the refused open took, and a declined lift hands the refusal to the stream's reader) and the withdrawn-plugin case (nothing more is sent). Lead verdict: pass, after the independent Opus r3 review (2026-11-19). Also pins the Face ID denial lift (`$liftDenials`): unary and stream lifts, the mount re-check after the lift, and the replay overflow re-checked after the lift (faceid-wire F30, F33).

Admission seam (C4): `openListener` opens additional listeners on the same routes, bound only to an OS-assigned port on `127.0.0.1` or to handed-in byte streams with TLS at the listener, never to a configured host or port. Each listener's gate decides every request and upgrade request before any route, upgrade handler or the fallback: a refusal dispatches nothing, a pass may carry the Peer resources receive, headers pinned through the route's own, and an `only` route outside which the gate's refusal answers. Dispatch moves into `dispatchRequest` and `dispatchUpgrade`, which the configured listener uses without a gate, so its behaviour is unchanged. Every upgrade socket of an additional listener gets its error handler and is tracked before the gate runs, a refused upgrade is destroyed once its refusal is written, and ids are reserved before the bind, so a reset or half-open refused client cannot crash the process or hold close open, and two opens of one id cannot both bind. A pass decision may carry a nonce, which the index renderer receives for that response through an async-local store. Lead verdict: keep, after two independent review rounds (2026-11-07); the lead reviews this file line by line before it merges. One-time launch tokens (C4): the `webserver/request` event is emitted for each request and upgrade request the main listener receives, before routing, so Connection can consume a launch token a request presents outside the exchanges; a listener that throws is logged and the request is routed regardless. Lead verdict for this change: approved, after an independent review of the change and its fixes (2026-11-10). Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; every listener answers 400 to a request or upgrade with more than one Host line, counted from the raw headers regardless of case, before any gate, route, upgrade handler or fallback runs.

S2 review of the /api trust fence: a Host header must be a bare authority — no user information, no whitespace or control character, no trailing dot (a repeated Host line is answered 400 by the web server before the fence runs) — and a state-changing request on the /api channel must carry the browser's own origin account (an Origin header, or Fetch-Metadata same-origin/none), while a route may accept a cross-site document navigation whose response the initiator's page cannot read. A state-changing /api request that carries neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is accepted toward a loopback Host or an HTTPS listener, where a Fetch-Metadata browser always sends a marker, and refused toward any other plain-HTTP destination; a marker that is present and not same-origin or none is refused. Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; the /api target is read with the same URL parse the router uses, so no dot-segment, percent-encoded or backslash spelling reaches /api without the origin rule, and a cross-site request is refused on every route. Protected home, read fence: a read or listing opens the target key and confirms the descriptor is the file or directory the key names before reading through it, so a read tool's protected-read check on the key covers the content when a component of the key is swapped for a link between the check and the open. On Linux the descriptor's `/proc/self/fd` path must equal the key and a listing reads its entries through that descriptor; elsewhere the descriptor's device and inode must equal the key's after the open and the key must still be its own realpath. A mismatch fails with `FS_IO_ERROR`. Reads open with `O_NONBLOCK` outside Windows so a FIFO swapped in after the regular-file check cannot block the open. Mutations: an edit's read and an overwrite's diff basis go through the same confirmed descriptor; every write, create, move and delete holds the target's directory open and confirms it. On Linux missing directories are created through the held parent's descriptor and held without following a link, the staging directory is held without following a link and confirmed private (owner, 0700) and empty, and the temp file, publication and removal are reached through `/proc/self/fd`; elsewhere directories are created by name and confirmed, and the staging directory and the published file are confirmed by path (removing a misplaced publication). A changed path fails with `FS_IO_ERROR`. The staging directory is removed without walking it (unlink the temp file, then a non-recursive `rmdir` that leaves a non-empty directory or a link in its name in place), and a misplaced one outside Linux only when empty. A listing leaves out a child link that resolves through itself (`ELOOP`) instead of failing. Content, errors and limits are otherwise upstream's. Lead verdict (2026-11-11): kept; on Linux every write, create, move, edit and delete reaches the target directory, the directories it creates and the staging directory through held descriptors opened without following links, and the staging directory is removed without recursion, so a link swapped in after the checks fails the mutation with FS_IO_ERROR; outside Linux the path checks are best effort as documented.

Network rules of a confined execution (C1 rule 19), new module: `RUNNER_NETWORK` says only bwrap can express `off` and `proxy`, both by a network namespace of its own holding only loopback. Under `proxy` the proxy's Unix socket is bound in at its own path and a bridge, run by the host's Node inside the sandbox before the command, listens on loopback port 3128 and forwards to the socket; `PROXY_ENVIRONMENT` names that port in the proxy variables and sets `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`. The bridge detaches before the command, which keeps the wrap's exit status, signals and descriptors. A failure the bridge reports, or a Node that cannot start (a `sandbox-proxy-bridge:` line and exit 1), is a runner failure and the command does not run. Lead verdict (2026-11-13): approved; stricter only, and the host network is unchanged while no resolver is mounted. The new `host` network form adds no bwrap argument (the host's namespace), and `networkRefusal` excludes it.

The optional network seam, new module: the `SandboxNetworkResolver` Service Definition (`ctx.sandboxNetwork`), a synchronous function from the call's session and workspace root to a `SandboxNetwork` or `undefined` for the host's network; a resolver that cannot decide answers the most restrictive network it supports. With none mounted no policy carries a network. Lead verdict (2026-11-13): approved; stricter only, and the host network is unchanged while no resolver is mounted.

A writer lock whose record is empty or lacks its newline for ten seconds is taken over, because only a writer killed between creating the file and writing its PID leaves one, and no PID probe can ever clear it. A takeover claim older than the same ten seconds is aged out too, because its claimant was killed before releasing it and the claim's name repeats for the same lock record. The ageing renames the claim to a unique name before deleting it and links a fresh claim back, so two contenders cannot both age one out, and a claimant re-checks that the claim at its name is still its own before it removes the lock. Reach route admission: builds a route's `admitPeer` from the reach policy for the action the route serves, so a device reaches an exact route only when the policy already allows that action. Before this, an exact route reached a non-owner peer only through the Gateway, which decides by path rather than by action, so a capability the policy allowed was refused. Fail-closed three ways: no action named, no resource named, or no remote access mounted all admit only the owner. No upstream action, parameter or export is removed or renamed. Lead verdict: kept; it adds the admission check the routes were missing and leaves the policy the single place an action is decided.

Reach route admission: the present route declares the action it serves so `peerAdmission` can decide a device against the reach policy, instead of the route being reachable only through the Gateway's path check. The route's own behaviour is unchanged; only the admission declaration is added. Lead verdict: kept; it is a declaration, not a behaviour change, and the policy still refuses the action it names where the action is denied.

Reach route admission: the export route asks the reach policy for the command call it serves, so a device that never held the unlock for `export` is refused the archive. The route previously reached every non-owner peer only through the Gateway, which decides by path rather than by action, so a capability the policy allowed was refused. No upstream action, parameter or export is removed or renamed. Lead verdict: kept; the change is the admission check the route was missing, and the policy remains the single place an action is decided.

No recorded Session, user material or network service supplies its content.

Long-chat load measurement: a phase-timed worker that runs the production open, read, Session restore, projection and first-history paths in a fresh process per scenario, and separately times the raw file read, frame decompression and JSONL parse, so a long chat's load time is attributed rather than guessed. It measures only; it changes no product behaviour.

Long-chat load measurement: compiles the measurement worker beside the other benchmark workers, so the timed code runs as plain Node against built package entries exactly as the other benchmark cases do.
